title: The land described
hookLine: jeweled trees, lotus ponds, birds whose songs are the teaching (Smaller Sukhavati-vyuha)

cards: Listen before you look. When the short sutra describes the land of bliss, it fills it with sound. Music drifts down from the sky.
A breeze moves through rows of jeweled trees, and they ring. And there are birds, swans, peacocks, parrots and others, singing by day and by night.
The Buddha tells Shariputra what they're singing, and it isn't only birdsong. The sutra lingers over every pond and branch. Today: the land described.

teach.b: Begin with the water. The land has lotus ponds of jewels, the sutra says, with clear water and golden sand covering the bottom.
The lotuses are as large as cart wheels, and each shines with the light of its own color: blue with blue light, yellow with yellow, red with red, white with white. Next, the trees and the sky.

teach.h: TREES THAT RING IN THE BREEZE.
teach.b: Rows of jeweled trees line the paths, hung with nets of bells, and when the breeze moves them, they sound like many instruments playing together. Flowers fall from the sky.
In the early morning, the people there gather them in their robes, carry them off to offer to Buddhas in other worlds, and come home in time for their meal. Then the birds.

What they sing is the teaching: the qualities and practices that lead to awakening, the path itself, in birdsong. Anyone who hears them begins to remember the Buddha, the teaching and the community. Last, the turn.
The Buddha tells Shariputra not to imagine these birds were born as birds because of past wrongdoing. In that land, he says, the lower realms don't exist, not even as a name.
Amitabha made the birds himself, so their songs would carry the teaching.

teach.h: NO BIRD THERE FOR PAST WRONGS.

teach.b: The water, the trees, the bells and the birds are all teachers.

how: Pure Land Buddhists chant the short sutra on the land of bliss in their services, and its pictures of lotus ponds, jeweled trees and singing birds appear in temple paintings and altar decorations.

o: the sutra's picture of the Pure Land, where all things teach
a garden the monks built at Shravasti for the Buddha
an earthly kingdom ruled by the king who became a monk

games.q: the land described: tap the pairs.
p: ring like music in the breeze
offered to Buddhas of other worlds

s: the birds in the land of bliss were born there for past wrongs
the Buddha says the lower realms don't exist there; Amitabha made the birds to spread the teaching.
each lotus shines with the light of its own color
blue with blue light, yellow with yellow, red with red, white with white.
the land of bliss is a silent place
it is full of sound: music from the sky, ringing trees and singing birds.

games.q: you're Shariputra. the Buddha has just told you about birds in the land of bliss. how did they get there?
o: they were born as birds because of past wrongdoing.
Amitabha made them, so their songs would carry the teaching.
they flew there from this world.
games.why: the sutra rules out the first answer directly: in that land the lower realms don't exist even as a name. the birds are teachers by design.

practice: If you can, open a window or step outside and listen for birds; if there are none, listen to whatever is there, a fan, traffic, rain, a neighbor's radio.
Don't name or judge the sounds; let each arrive the way the sutra's birds do, as if saying something simple: this, now, wake up. When the mind wanders, let the next sound bring you back.

wordCard.voice: The land described: lotus ponds shining in their own colors, jeweled trees that ring in the breeze, flowers from the sky, and birds whose songs are the teaching. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: Sukhavati-vyuha, the title of the sutras, rendered 'the array of the land of bliss'.

carryVoice: Your line: the birds teach. Even the lotuses shine with their own light. Twelve fifty-nine, done.

sources.ref: Smaller Sukhavati-vyuha (the ponds, lotuses, trees, flowers and birds of the land)
